title: OpenAI Internal Model Formalizes a Modulus Proof of Cannon’s Conjecture in Lean 4
aiSystem: OpenAI Internal Frontier Math Model + Lean 4
whyItMatters: Formally proves James Cannon’s 1994 conjecture in Lean 4 + Comparator: every word-hyperbolic group with Gromov boundary S² acts properly and cocompactly by isometries on hyperbolic 3-space ℍ³.
summary: In family 246 of OpenAI’s formal math repository (CannonGeometricAction.lean), an internal OpenAI frontier reasoning model produced and machine-verified a modulus-based Lean 4 + Comparator proof of Cannon’s Conjecture (1994)—one of the flagship open problems of geometric group theory and 3-manifold topology. The formalized theorem proves that every Gromov word-hyperbolic group whose visual boundary is homeomorphic to the 2-sphere S² admits a proper, cocompact isometric action on ℍ³ with finite kernel.
technicalHighlights: Targets Cannon’s 1994 Conjecture (32 years open), a foundational bridge between Gromov hyperbolic groups and Thurston’s geometrization of 3-manifolds.
Uses a discrete conformal modulus argument formalized end-to-end in Lean 4 with Comparator challenge specification (CannonGeometricAction.lean).
Proves existence of a proper cocompact isometric action on ℍ³ with finite kernel for any word-hyperbolic group with S² boundary.
caveats: Released inside OpenAI’s unrefereed github.com/openai/math collection; while Lean 4 + Comparator checks kernel soundness, human specialist audit of the formal definitions (Gromov boundary and hyperbolic action) remains essential.

scoreRationale.verification: Machine-checked in Lean 4 with Comparator challenge files, though external specialist definition audits are still ongoing.
